title.narrative: HPN - Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (MEDS) USAID Supply Chain Strengthening (KEMSA follow on)

description.narrative: (Kenya): .Using FY 2022 funds, USAID will support the Supply Chain Strengthening activity to warehouse and distribute health commodities funded by the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and President's Malaria Initiative (PMI). The activity will be implemented by the Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (MEDS), a Christian not-for-profit organization whose functions include the warehousing and distribution of medications and medical supplies. Under this activity, MEDS will manage warehousing and distribution for PEPFAR commodities and PMI-procured malaria rapid diagnostic tests, malaria medicines and insecticide-treated nets from the central warehouse to public sector health facilities nationwide. USAID will also support through this activity the procurement, warehousing and distribution of vayu - bCPAP machines to health facilities providing maternal and newborn care in USAID counties. The vayu - bCPAP machine is an evidence based life saving solution to addressing newborn deaths caused by prematurity and low birth weight. This intervention, complemented by other health system strengthening strategies, will contribute to the reduction of neonatal mortality to fewer than 10 per 1000 live births per the targets established in the Every Newborn Action Plan (ENP)..Generally speaking, USAID investments in MEDS will strengthen local health sector capacity to manage complex supply chain systems. This serves to build more stable and capable local systems which in turn boosts U.S national security objectives and improves public opinions of the United States in Kenya, as well as asserting U.S. influence and leadership in global health..
